strengths: The paper addresses an important and timely problem: few-shot novel view synthesis in extrapolative, pose-free settings while also producing aligned geometry.
weaknesses: The evaluation is not yet convincing enough for a top-tier acceptance. The paper claims state-of-the-art performance, but key comparisons are limited or incomplete, especially against recent generative and large view synthesis models; LVSM is only compared qualitatively.

strengths: The paper tackles an important and timely problem: pose-free few-shot novel-view synthesis with jointly generated appearance and geometry, especially under extrapolative viewpoints.
The overall warping-and-inpainting formulation is plausible, and combining off-the-shelf geometry prediction with diffusion-based completion is a reasonable direction.

The proposed proximity-based mesh conditioning and multi-view aggregated attention are potentially useful engineering components, and the reported ablations show incremental gains from the main modules.
The manuscript includes both single-view and multi-view experiments, plus qualitative examples of generated geometry, which is more ambitious than evaluating RGB synthesis alone.
weaknesses: The central technical claim around cross-modal attention instillation is not convincingly specified or validated. The method says image attention maps replace geometry attention maps, but then claims the image branch receives deterministic training signals from geometry; this causal story is unclear and internally inconsistent.

The evaluation is not strong enough for a top-tier acceptance. Several key contemporary generative NVS baselines are missing or only qualitatively compared, e.g. CAT3D/SV3D/Gen3C/Reconfusion-style methods, and LVSM is only shown qualitatively rather than in the main quantitative tables.

The geometry evaluation is weak and partly self-referential: pseudo ground-truth geometry is produced by VGGT, while VGGT is also used for conditioning. This makes the reported geometry quality hard to interpret as true 3D accuracy.

The paper’s claimed strength is image-geometry alignment, but there is no direct quantitative alignment metric, no user/perceptual study, and no rigorous reconstruction-quality evaluation against real geometry where available.

Several experimental details are confusing or contradictory. The appendix says training uses 3 reference views plus 1 target, while Table 4 claims the model was trained in a two-view setting; the learning rate is written as 1x10 with no exponent; and the description of Marigold/VGGT supervision is under-specified.

Ablations are limited. The improvement from cross-modal instillation is modest, and there is no careful ablation of attention direction, sharing during training versus inference, mesh filtering choices, VGGT dependence, or failure modes under erroneous poses/geometries.

The extrapolative-view definition is mathematically loose for SE(3), and the sampling protocols for DTU/RealEstate10K are not detailed enough to rule out cherry-picking or ensure comparability with baselines.

Presentation and polish are below the expected bar: there are incorrect dataset citations in captions/tables, wrong method reference numbers in figures, typos, awkward phrasing, an unfinished appendix table labeled 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled,' and repeated boilerplate captions.

Reproducibility appears limited: no code/model release details, insufficient architecture/training hyperparameters, unclear dataset splits, unclear baseline evaluation protocol, and no compute/runtime discussion.
The paper overclaims state-of-the-art performance despite narrow quantitative evidence, incomplete comparisons, and several inconsistencies that reduce confidence in the reported results.

strengths: The paper addresses an important and timely problem: pose-free few-shot novel view synthesis with both RGB and geometry generation, including difficult extrapolative views rather than only interpolation.

The core formulation is compelling: using predicted pointmaps for warping/inpainting, extending the setup to geometry completion, and enforcing image-geometry alignment through cross-modal attention instillation is a meaningful and technically plausible contribution.

The method is evaluated on multiple datasets/settings, including RealEstate10K, Co3D, and zero-shot DTU, with both extrapolative and interpolative splits. The reported gains in extrapolative settings are substantial, especially in LPIPS and SSIM.

The ablation study supports the contribution of the proposed components: pointmap conditioning, proximity-based mesh conditioning, and cross-modal attention instillation each improve performance progressively.
The paper has useful qualitative evidence showing aligned image and geometry outputs, and the ability to synthesize plausible unobserved regions is visually convincing in several examples.
weaknesses: The experimental section has notable polish and consistency issues. Table 5 is explicitly marked incomplete, and there are apparent inconsistencies about whether the model is trained with two-view, three-reference-view, or four-view sampling. These undermine confidence in the submission readiness.

The comparison set is somewhat incomplete for the central claims. LVSM is only compared qualitatively, and several strong generative or 3D-aware diffusion baselines are not quantitatively evaluated. This makes the claimed state-of-the-art status less fully supported.

The extrapolative-view definition is not mathematically rigorous as stated, since convex combinations in SE(3) are not directly well-defined. The actual split construction should be specified more operationally and reproducibly.

Geometry evaluation relies heavily on pseudo-ground-truth geometry from VGGT, which is also used by the method for conditioning. This risks circularity and makes it hard to assess true 3D accuracy, especially for completed/inpainted regions.

Some claims are stronger than the evidence. For example, the paper claims robust arbitrary-view and arbitrary-number-of-input generalization, but the quantitative evidence is limited and sometimes mostly qualitative.

Reproducibility is weaker than expected for a top-tier submission: the project page appears blank in the PDF, implementation details contain typos or missing values such as an incomplete learning rate exponent, and important training/evaluation details are underspecified.

The writing is generally understandable but contains many grammatical errors, citation mistakes, and repeated generic figure captions, which reduce clarity and make some technical details harder to verify.

strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem: pose-free few-shot novel view synthesis with extrapolative views and explicit geometry completion.
The core idea of jointly inpainting image and pointmap geometry, with cross-modal attention instillation between the image and geometry branches, is technically plausible and well motivated.

The paper includes comparisons across several relevant settings and datasets, including DTU zero-shot, RealEstate10K in-domain, Co3D qualitative results, and additional comparisons to larger view-synthesis models.
Ablations isolate the main components: pointmap conditioning, proximity-based mesh conditioning, and cross-modal attention instillation, with consistent incremental gains.
The method has practical appeal because it produces both novel-view RGB images and aligned geometry without per-scene NeRF/3DGS optimization, and reported inference time is reasonable.
weaknesses: The novelty is moderate rather than clearly strong: the method combines warping-and-inpainting, reference U-Nets, diffusion inpainting, external geometry predictors, and attention sharing in a sensible way, but many ingredients are inherited from recent work.

The evaluation relies heavily on an external geometry/pose predictor, especially VGGT, but the dependence is not disentangled sufficiently. It is unclear how much of the gain comes from the proposed model versus the strength of the geometry prior and pseudo-ground-truth geometry.

The pose-free claim needs sharper formulation. The method still requires a target camera viewpoint in a coordinate system compatible with predicted reference geometry, and the paper does not fully clarify how arbitrary target poses are specified in genuinely unposed scenarios.

Geometry evaluation is comparatively weak. The paper emphasizes aligned 3D completion, but most evidence is qualitative or based on pseudo geometry; stronger metrics against true depth/3D ground truth and alignment error would be needed to support the central geometry claims.

Several comparisons are incomplete or potentially unfair. Some strong generative NVS/3D methods are discussed only qualitatively or in the appendix, and the baselines may not all receive equally favorable geometry, camera, or inference-time assumptions.
The robustness claims are overstated: Tables 5 and 6 show noticeable degradation under noise and sparsity, especially in SSIM and LPIPS, despite the text describing minimal degradation.

The ablation gains for the proposed components are relatively small in absolute terms, particularly for proximity-based mesh conditioning and cross-modal instillation, making the significance of each component somewhat modest.

Reproducibility details contain ambiguities and apparent errors, such as the learning rate written as 1×10 without an exponent, and several implementation choices around mesh construction, target pose sampling, and training losses are underspecified.
Writing and presentation are generally understandable but have recurring terminology inconsistencies, typos, and overclaims, which make it harder to assess the exact technical contribution.

strengths: The paper targets an important and timely problem: pose-free or pose-light few-shot novel view synthesis with aligned image and geometry generation, especially for extrapolative views.

The proposed warping-and-inpainting formulation with explicit pointmap conditioning, mesh-based filtering, and a paired image/geometry diffusion setup is a coherent direction and could be useful if validated rigorously.

The manuscript includes several quantitative tables, ablations over major components, and experiments across multiple datasets including DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D, and qualitative out-of-domain examples.
weaknesses: The central technical claim around cross-modal attention instillation is not fully convincing. The described mechanism appears mainly to inject image attention into the geometry branch, but the text claims bidirectional synergistic benefits and deterministic geometry signals regularizing image generation; this causal pathway is not clearly specified or demonstrated.

The evaluation is not sufficiently rigorous for the strength of the claims. Geometry quality is largely supervised/evaluated through pseudo-ground-truth from VGGT rather than true 3D ground truth, which makes claims about aligned geometry and 3D completion difficult to trust.

The comparisons are potentially unfair or incomplete. The paper compares against feedforward methods, warping methods, and large generative models under mixed one-view/two-view settings, but does not provide enough detail on retraining, input protocol matching, target pose availability, or hyperparameter tuning for baselines.

The term “pose-free” is overstated. The method depends heavily on an external geometry/pose predictor and a specified target camera; performance may be dominated by VGGT quality, yet the paper does not isolate this dependency sufficiently.

Several claims are stronger than the evidence. Extrapolative view synthesis is evaluated with PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS against single ground-truth images despite requiring hallucination of unseen regions, and the paper does not include human preference, perceptual consistency, or multi-view geometric consistency metrics that would better support the generative claims.

Ablations are too limited. The component ablation shows modest gains, but there is no strong isolation of attention instillation versus simply using shared conditioning, no comparison to alternative cross-modal fusion strategies, and limited analysis of failure cases.

Reproducibility is weak. Important training details are missing or inconsistent, such as an apparent malformed learning rate, unclear training view counts across main text and appendix, limited dataset sampling details, and no released code/weights at submission time.

The paper contains presentation and consistency issues, including typos, citation mistakes, inconsistent naming of attention distillation/instillation, and table formatting errors, which reduce confidence in the care of the experimental protocol.

The qualitative results are visually emphasized, but many figures are small and hard to inspect, and the paper provides little systematic analysis of where the method fails, especially under inaccurate external geometry, large occlusions, nonrigid scenes, or domain shifts.

Overall, while the direction is plausible and there are some positive empirical signals, the evidence does not adequately establish novelty, technical soundness, or fair state-of-the-art performance at the level expected for a top-tier AI conference.

strengths: The paper tackles an important and timely problem: pose-free sparse-view novel view synthesis with extrapolation, while also producing aligned geometry rather than only RGB outputs.

The core idea is appealing and reasonably novel: formulating both image and pointmap prediction as warping-and-inpainting, then using cross-modal attention instillation to align the image and geometry branches.
The method is technically coherent and well motivated. Proximity-based mesh conditioning is a practical addition that addresses noisy point-cloud projections from external geometry predictors.

The empirical results are encouraging, especially in extrapolative settings where the method substantially outperforms feedforward baselines on RealEstate10K and DTU, and the ablations show consistent gains from pointmap conditioning, mesh conditioning, and cross-modal instillation.

The paper includes useful qualitative evidence, robustness tests, runtime discussion, and comparisons to both classical sparse-view NVS baselines and recent large-model systems such as LVSM and ViewCrafter.
weaknesses: The method relies heavily on VGGT or similar external geometry and pose predictors, both for conditioning and for pseudo ground-truth geometry supervision. This makes it hard to disentangle the contribution of the proposed diffusion model from the strength and failure modes of the external geometry model.

The geometry evaluation is not fully convincing. Since target geometry supervision is pseudo-labeled by VGGT rather than true 3D ground truth in many experiments, claims about accurate 3D completion and geometric alignment are somewhat stronger than the evidence supports.

Some comparisons may be imperfectly balanced. The method is trained on RealEstate10K/Co3D/MVImgNet, while several baselines are not necessarily optimized for the same extrapolative protocol; the paper should specify splits, sample counts, target selection, and baseline adaptation details more rigorously.

The extrapolative-view definition based only on camera-position convex hull ignores viewing direction and scene visibility, so the difficulty of extrapolation may vary substantially across datasets and examples.
The robustness claims are overstated: Tables 5 and 6 show noticeable degradation under noise and sparsity, even if performance remains usable.

Reproducibility is incomplete at submission time: code and weights are only promised, and several important training details are either missing or unclear, including the apparent learning-rate typo in the appendix.

The qualitative results are strong, but the paper would benefit from more systematic evaluation of perceptual plausibility and multi-view consistency, especially for hallucinated unseen regions where PSNR/SSIM against a single target view may not fully capture correctness.
